passage: Most stars form in clusters, and astronomers once assumed that the Sun did too. Supporting this idea, some meteorites contain traces of iron-60, a radioactive isotope produced in exploding massive stars and found only in the early solar system. Iron-60 decays quickly, so it must have reached the young solar system soon after being made. However, other researchers note that iron-60 can also be carried long distances by stellar winds. Therefore, the presence of iron-60 in meteorites ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: does not by itself establish that the Sun formed close to a massive star in a cluster.
proves that the early solar system formed far from any massive or exploding stars.
shows that stellar winds produce more iron-60 than exploding massive stars do.
suggests that iron-60 decays much more slowly than astronomers previously thought.
steps: Iron-60 was used as evidence that a massive star was nearby (a cluster).
But stellar winds can carry it far, so it might have come from a distant star.
So iron-60 alone doesn't settle the question.
Proving the opposite, comparing amounts or changing the decay rate goes beyond the text.
key: When an alternative explanation is raised, the logical conclusion is usually that the evidence is not decisive.
